summary: Guidance to separate burst capacity for realtime inference vs nightly batch embeddings to avoid tenant-wide 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lexicon Labs reports repeated 429 throttles across their dedicated tenant after migrating their nightly embedding backfill to run concurrently with low-latency realtime inference traffic. The customer expects background batch jobs to consume a separate quota or burst allowance so realtime API keys remain healthy during spikes.

Impact:
- Several realtime endpoints (chat generation) receive intermittent 429s between 03:00-06:00 UTC during nightly embedding windows.
- User-visible latency and failed requests for live product features.
- Customer requests recommended configuration changes and guidance to avoid tenant-wide token exhaustion while preserving cost predictability.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) - tenant: lexicon-prod
- Region: us-east (single region dedicated nodes)
- Reproducible during nightly embedding pipelines that enqueue ~750 concurrent embedding requests in short bursts; realtime traffic baseline ~40 qps with short bursts to 120 qps.
- Model types: embedding-small-v1 (batch workers), gptx-lite-8k (realtime).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Trigger embedding backfill job using their in-house uploader that opens 150 parallel workers each issuing concurrent /embeddings calls with 5-second TTL keys.
2. Start a load test of realtime endpoint: 40 qps steady, occasional 2s spikes to 120 qps.
3. Observe 429 responses on realtime generation endpoints within the first 5-10 minutes of the batch start.

Observed behavior:
- 429 payload: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after_ms": 12000}
- Token counters on customer side show background workers exhausting tenant tokens quickly.
- Logs include edge request IDs: rwd-edge-req-20260310-2a7c, rwd-edge-req-20260310-2a8f.

Expected behavior:
- Background long-running batch jobs should be able to be scheduled with a separate quota (or throttled) so realtime traffic does not incur 429s, or customers should receive prescriptive config to ensure realtime keys maintain headroom.

Attachments:
- embedding_job_config.yaml (customer provided snippet)
- sample curl reproducer and aggregated request timing CSV
- Grafana screenshots (token consumption, 429 rate)

investigation_notes: Tenant-global accounting confirmed: token consumption is aggregated across keys on dedicated pool when tenant-level quota is configured.
Rate-limiter behavior: per-key soft limits exist but do not reserve headroom; background bursts can still drive tenant tokens to zero and trigger 429s on realtime keys.
Edge logs show simultaneous increase in new connections from embedding workers at 03:42 UTC; CPU on rate-limiter pods spiked by 38% and token counters dropped to zero within 90s of batch start.

Workarounds evaluated: separate tenant assignment (requires infra change), server-side per-key throttles (applied), client-side concurrency reduction (recommended), scheduling staggered embeddings (recommended).
Engineering enhancement: 'traffic_class' + reservable headroom per class (tracked in backlog, linked PR).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied: created/annotated 'lexicon-batch' key and enforced a server-side soft limit of 8000 tokens/min and label 'low-priority'. Customer instructed to reduce concurrent workers from 150 to 25 with jitter; provided SDK/curl config snippets. Monitoring monitored overnight; initial signal shows realtime 429s dropped to zero during the next embedding window (customer to confirm). Long-term: engineering will evaluate quota partitioning and a 'traffic_class' reservation feature (linked PR). Follow-ups: schedule architecture review with Lexicon Labs to discuss dedicated pool sizing and split-tenancy options. Ticket remains open pending customer confirmation after next nightly run.
